children: Roivant Sciences stock surged after the biotech said Tuesday that its experimental treatment met the mid-stage trial's main goal for patients with high blood pressure in arteries of the lungs and heart.

Roivant has been evaluating mosliciguat as a first-of-its-kind treatment for pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease, a serious, progressive condition. The trial enrolled 135 patients across 20 countries.
Roivant stock jumped 20% to $41.83 on Tuesday. Shares of the biotechnology company have surged 90% this year, far outpacing the broader market.

Mosliciguat, which is a dry powder ingested once a day using an inhaler, was more effective than a placebo at lowering pressure and resistance in lung blood vessels after 16 weeks of treatment. The drug helped patients walk farther in a six-minute test, Roivant said. After 24 weeks of treatment, patients walked 52.7 meters farther than those on the placebo.

Researchers noted no significant side effects. Only about 12% of patients taking mosliciguat reported a cough, compared to 18% of those on the placebo treatment. Coughing is a typical and notorious side effect of inhaled treatments for pulmonary hypertension, often forcing patients to quit treatment.
Jefferies analysts described the mid-stage trial as "much better than expectations." They maintained a Buy rating on the shares and raised their price target to $52 from $42.

Patients with interstitial lung disease develop pulmonary hypertension when scarring damages blood vessels in the lungs, making it harder for the heart to pump blood. Across the U.S. and Europe, up to 200,000 patients are living with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease, and they have limited or no approved treatment options, Roivant said.
Current treatments available for the condition include inhaled treprostinil products and off-label uses of medications that relax blood vessels and improve blood flow.
Roivant said mosliciguat has already entered into a late-stage study required for regulatory approval.
